title: How Claude Bernard's Washed Liver and Curare Frogs Discovered the Internal Sea — Claude Bernard's 1855 Washed-Liver Glycogen & Curare Frogs, 4.5-g Blood Glucose 45-Min Buffer vs. 90-g Hepatic Reserve, Cannon's Homeostasis, Maltese Canine GSD Ia G6PC & Feline Hepatic Lipidosis Refeeding PO₄³⁻

teenKit.tldr: A 21-year-old rejected playwright discovered that our bodies maintain a hidden, internal ocean of chemical balance to keep us alive between meals. By washing a dog's liver and experimenting with curare frogs, Claude Bernard unlocked the invisible world of metabolism and homeostasis.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Without this discovery, we would have no modern understanding of how conditions like diabetes, hypoglycemia, or metabolic disorders operate invisibly behind the scenes of a seemingly healthy body.
keyTakeaways: Metabolism is an invisible, ever-shifting balance of chemicals and energy that cannot be seen on a standard X-ray.
Claude Bernard proved that the liver acts as a massive energy reserve (glycogen), storing fuel to protect your blood sugar between meals.
The concept of 'homeostasis' means our internal environment stays remarkably stable even when the external world changes drastically.

vocab.meaning: The continuous network of chemical reactions inside your cells that keeps you alive, transforms food into energy, and powers every heartbeat.
The body's automatic, self-regulating process of maintaining a stable internal environment despite external chaos or changes.
A complex starch-like sugar stored primarily in the liver and muscles that acts as the body's short-term energy reserve.
A powerful plant-derived poison historically used by indigenous groups and scientists to study muscle action and nerve signaling.

quiz.question: What kind of diagnostic landscape do doctors face when trying to analyze metabolism and cellular energy?
options: A crystal-clear structural view visible on every standard X-ray
An invisible muddy water of dissolved chemicals, hormones, and enzymes
A purely mechanical system identical to a broken bone
A static blueprint that never changes over time
quiz.explanation: Unlike a broken bone, metabolic issues happen at a microscopic level with invisible chemical balances rather than structural cracks.

quiz.question: Who originally uncovered the foundational principles of modern experimental physiology discussed in the episode?
options: A decorated aristocratic physician with decades of hospital experience
A 21-year-old rejected playwright turned scientist named Claude Bernard
An orthopedic surgeon specializing in X-ray technology
A nineteenth-century pharmacist who only studied plant poisons
quiz.explanation: Claude Bernard famously transitioned from a failed playwright to a groundbreaking scientist who revolutionized physiology.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of the hepatic (liver) glycogen reserve discovered through Bernard's washed-liver experiments?
options: To filter out plant toxins like curare from the bloodstream
To produce rigid structural bones in place of calcium
To act as a glucose buffer that maintains blood sugar stability between meals
To generate electrical signals directly for the nervous system
quiz.explanation: The liver stores glycogen as a vital energy buffer to keep blood sugar stable when you are not eating.
